item.text: {"text":"Search results support text enrichment and feature gating separately, but did not establish a verified 2024–2026 NextItNet method combining both with a title/description encoder trained from scratch. [ITS-Rec (2025)](https://www.mdpi.com/2079-9292/14/9/1748) incorporates titles, descriptions and reviews into sequential recommendation, but uses pretrained BERT and a SASRec-derived backbone; its strongest reported textual contribution comes from reviews, unavailable here. [DWSRec (2024)](https://ojs.aaai.org/index.php/AAAI/article/view/28786) also depends on pretrained text embeddings. Neither directly validates the proposed constrained architecture. [Hierarchical Gating Networks](https://arxiv.org/abs/1906.09217) provides an older precedent for selecting item features through feature-level and instance-level gates, without establishing title/description-specific compatibility.\n\nA compatible experimental hypothesis: tokenize available titles/descriptions, learn randomly initialized token embeddings with mean pooling or a small text CNN, and jointly train a text-conditioned gate inside the existing NextItNet network. Fuse the gated text representation with item embeddings before causal dilated residual convolutions; use the same jointly learned item representation for candidate scoring. This preserves [NextItNet’s causal convolutional backbone](https://fajieyuan.github.io/papers/nextitnet6.pdf) and permits one checkpoint per category without an independent semantic scorer. This is a proposed adaptation, not a demonstrated result from the retrieved papers. Compare ID-only, ungated text fusion and gated text fusion using fixed validation HR@10; shuffled-text ablation can test whether improvements depend on product information rather than additional parameters."}
